lines.text: The layers shape the agent. A few features shape each session.
Four worth knowing on day one: steer, undo, inspect, and run in parallel.
Shift+Tab cycles the permission modes: auto, manual, accept edits, and plan.
lines.say: Shift tab cycles the permission modes: auto, manual, accept edits, and plan.

lines.text: Auto is the default in the terminal:|a classifier blocks risky actions instead of asking.
Plan mode explores and writes a plan,|without touching your source files until you approve it.
Press Escape twice, or type /rewind,|to restore the code, the conversation, or both.
lines.say: Press escape twice, or type slash rewind, to restore the code, the conversation, or both.

lines.text: It won't undo files that only shell commands changed,|and it's no replacement for git.
Checkpoints are saved with the conversation, so rewind still works after you resume.
/context shows what loaded, and what each part costs.
lines.say: Slash context shows what loaded, and what each part costs.

lines.text: It also suggests what to trim when a tool or a memory file gets heavy.
/doctor runs a checkup of your installation, settings and rules files.
lines.say: Slash doctor runs a checkup of your installation, settings and rules files.

lines.text: Check both before you blame the model.
Start with --worktree, and each session gets its own checkout,|so parallel work doesn't collide.
lines.say: Start with dash dash worktree, and each session gets its own checkout, so parallel work doesn't collide.

lines.text: Then subagents for side tasks, agent view to watch background sessions,|and agent teams, still experimental, for agents that coordinate.
Codex has the same ideas:|/permissions for approvals and the sandbox, and /review for a second look at your changes.
lines.say: Codex has the same ideas: slash permissions for approvals and the sandbox, and slash review for a second look at your changes.
